_readme: Every state (plus DC) classified by what statewide vacancy data it publishes, and why it is or is not on the dashboard. Every entry was checked directly by this project (see 'protocol'); 'checked' says how: 'direct' = read the agency's (or publisher's) own page or document; 'secondary' = the primary source could not be read automatically and the classification rests on news coverage or a legislative summary of it. 'evidence' lists what was read. 'lpi' records how the Learning Policy Institute's July 2026 scan classified the state, as a cross-check only. Re-check annually.
protocol: 1. Search the state education agency's own website for vacancy or unfilled-position data (site-restricted search).
2. Search more broadly for statewide figures from other publishers: state boards, legislatures, university partners, associations, unions (recorded as non-agency).
3. Open any source found and record what it counts, when, and against what denominator.
4. Classify: included / candidate / counts / different / collects / none, and record evidence links and the date.
5. Compare with the Learning Policy Institute's annual scan and resolve any disagreement by reading the primary source.

cross_check.label: Learning Policy Institute, State Teacher Shortages 2026 Update (July 2026)

categories.candidate: Publishes a rate or a same-source denominator, but not added yet (reason given)
categories.counts: Publishes statewide vacancy counts, but no rate or denominator from the same source
categories.different: Publishes a figure that measures something different (job postings, positions not filled by fully licensed staff, projected hires)
categories.collects: Collects vacancy data (or has begun to), but no published statewide figures were found

states.what: Oct 1 unfilled FTE by category with filled FTE; published rate
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot with a same-source denominator, multi-year.

states.what: Fall unfilled FTE / total available FTE (published rate)
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot, published rate, multi-year.

states.what: Beginning-of-year vacancies and authorized FTE (CERRA)
states.reason: Start-of-year snapshot with same-source denominator; includes service staff (flagged).

states.what: 12-month count of full-time postings unfilled or filled by substitutes, / employed teachers
states.reason: Published rate, multi-year; shown as a different measure.

states.what: Positions unfilled all year / all teaching positions
states.reason: Published rate, multi-year; shown as a different measure.

states.what: Vacant and 'unfilled' counts (no denominator)
states.reason: Shown as counts only; illustrates vacant vs. not-fully-qualified.

states.what: Fall share of teaching FTE 'vacant' in district personnel records (REP), from the statutory EPIC/MSU Michigan Teacher Shortage Study: 2.8% in fall 2024. 'Vacant' means a funded position that is unfilled or temporarily assigned to a substitute, temporary employee or outside contractor, including positions held for staff on leave or on loan. Positions held by under-credentialed teachers count as filled and are measured separately.
states.reason: On the dashboard as a start-of-year snapshot, using the rate published in the statutory Michigan Teacher Shortage Study. It also counts positions held for staff on leave, which other snapshot states do not.

states.what: OSSE annual Faculty & Staff Data Collection: vacant teacher FTE as of the October enrollment-audit date (about Oct. 5), published in yearly vacancy files: 288 (2022-23), 362 (2023-24), 169 (2024-25), 193.5 (2025-26). The same collection's counts files give citywide teacher headcounts: 8,357, 8,767, 8,939 and 9,145. Computed as vacant FTE ÷ (headcount + vacant FTE): about 3.3%, 4.0%, 1.9% and 2.1%.
states.reason: The definition is a snapshot of vacant teaching positions on a fixed date and is not based on credentials; long-term substitutes employed four weeks or more are reported as staff on the roster, which suggests substitute-covered positions are not counted as vacant, though OSSE does not say so explicitly. All four years now have both components from the same collection, but OSSE publishes no rate, vacancies are FTE while teachers are headcounts (which understates a rate somewhat, since part-time teachers count as one), the 2024-25 file rounds vacant FTE to whole numbers, the files note that vacancy counts include only LEAs and schools that reported vacancies, and DC is a single city rather than a state.

evidence.label: OSSE educator workforce data (vacancy files by year)
OSSE Faculty and Staff Data Collection Policy Guidance (vacancy definition)
OSSE 2022-23 counts and demographics file (teacher headcount)
OSSE 2024-25 counts and demographics file (teacher headcount)

states.what: ADE Teacher Shortage Impact survey of LEAs (late summer): FTE teaching positions LEAs are 'actively seeking to fill through traditional hiring methods' (1,387 of 57,567 planned FTE, about 2.4%, in September 2025; 1,385 of just over 48,000, 'almost 3%', in August 2024). Reported separately: positions covered by stopgaps such as long-term substitutes, contracted staff, 6/5 contracts and student teachers (4,242, or 7%, in 2025).
states.reason: The actively-recruiting measure is not defined by credentials (it is narrower than Illinois's, which also counts substitute-covered positions), so it is not excluded on those grounds. But it is a voluntary survey whose coverage changed a lot (269 LEAs, about 60%, in 2024; 523, 83%, in 2025), the reports do not say whether actively recruited positions overlap with stopgap-covered ones, and the denominator is planned positions among respondents only.

evidence.label: ADE Teacher Shortage Impact Report, Fall 2025
ADE Teacher Shortage Impact Report, Fall 2024 (updated Nov 2025)
ADE ERR dashboards and survey data

states.what: DDOE Excellent Educator Hiring Practices (Talent Practices) Survey of district HR leads: 259 positions (189 instructional, 70 non-instructional) unfilled at the end of the February-October 2024 hiring season, about 2.5% of 10,178 instructional and non-instructional staff; the 19 school districts only, because charter data were incomplete.
states.reason: Not defined by credentials, but the summary gives no definition of 'unfilled' beyond the end of the hiring season, pools non-instructional staff in the published rate, and covers districts but not charters. No 2025 edition found.

evidence.label: Delaware hiring practices survey 2024, executive summary

states.what: Nevada Report Card personnel indicator required by NRS 385A.230: teacher vacancies, 'not filled by a teacher who has a contract to teach at the school on a full-time basis' (2,881 in 2024-25, as reported at the end of the year, per LPI's 2026 scan). The current statute defines a vacancy as 'an unfilled position, including, without limitation, any positions that are filled by a substitute teacher' or an outside contractor. The Report Card also publishes teacher counts (27,421 teachers and other licensed personnel in 2024-25).
states.reason: The definition is about whether a position has a contracted full-time teacher, not about credentials, and counting substitute-covered positions is comparable to Illinois, Michigan, and Pennsylvania. But the timing is unclear (reported at the end of the year, so it may not be a point-in-time count), the vacancy figure could not be located on the Report Card portal and is confirmed only through LPI, no rate is published, and the Report Card's teacher count also includes other licensed personnel such as counselors and nurses.

states.what: PDE Professional Staff Vacancy collection (PIMS), as of October 1 (October 2 in 2023): classroom teacher vacancies 2,156 (2023-24; 2,112 full-time, 44 part-time), 1,869 (2024-25) and 1,659 (2025-26). PDE's Professional Staff Summary gives classroom teachers on the same snapshot dates: 126,069, 126,816 and 128,699. Computed as vacancies ÷ (teachers + vacancies): about 1.7%, 1.5% and 1.3%.
states.reason: On the dashboard as a start-of-year snapshot. The rate is computed here from PDE's October vacancy count and its classroom-teacher count on the same date.

evidence.label: PDE professional and support personnel data (vacancy files and staff summaries)
PDE 2025-26 professional staff vacancy report, Q1 (definitions)

states.what: CSDE Biannual Educator Vacancy Survey (August and February): budgeted positions districts and approved private special education programs are actively working to fill. August teacher vacancies (special education plus all other teachers): 1,148.9 (2023-24), 1,220.5 (2024-25), 910.8 (2025-26), 819.7 (2026-27). Special services and paraeducators are reported separately.
states.reason: The definition, 'budgeted positions that districts are actively working to fill,' is not credential-based and is narrower than Illinois's, which also counts substitute-covered positions without active recruitment. It is not on the page because no rate is published and teacher staffing comes from a different EdSight collection, the August survey is taken before school starts, it covers responding districts only, and it includes private special education programs. (An earlier version of this entry cited 795 for August 2025, which does not match the dashboard.)

states.what: MSDE Annual Vacancy Data Collection: teacher vacancies at the beginning of the school year: 1,615.0 (2021-22), 2,144.9 (2022-23), 1,941.4 (2023-24), 1,619.0 (2024-25), 886.2 (2025-26). The same State Board presentation gives 64,191 teachers as of October 2025 (MSDE Staff Data Collection) and reports conditionally licensed teachers separately (6,177 positions in 2024-25).
states.reason: Vacancies are reported separately from conditionally licensed teachers, so the measure is not credential-based, and MSDE publishes a teacher count from its own staff collection. But the presentation does not define a vacancy or give its exact date, teacher totals for earlier years still need to be located, and no rate is published.

evidence.label: MSDE Teacher Workforce Supply and Demand, State Board, Feb 2026

states.what: FLDOE: teacher vacancies reported by districts at the start of the school year: 5,208 (2022-23) and 4,776 (2023-24, first day); later releases give only changes (13.3% lower on the first day of 2024-25, 1.11 vacancies per school; 17.7% lower for 2025-26, announced July 31, 2025). Separately, the Florida Education Association counts vacancies posted on district websites each August and January (e.g., 6,920 teacher postings in August 2023).
states.reason: FLDOE's count is an agency count, but it publishes no definition beyond 'vacancies' reported by subject, endorsement area and grade level, no denominator, and no counts after 2023-24, and the timing varies (first day in 2023 and 2024; before the school year in 2025). The FEA figures are job postings compiled by the teachers' union.

states.what: KDE Educator Shortage Survey (100% of districts): 671 certified teacher vacancies as of Sept 1, 2025
states.reason: Agency counts at a fixed date (Sept. 1); KDE's coverage does not define a vacancy or say how positions covered by substitutes or emergency-certified teachers (401 emergency certificates as of Sept. 1, 2025) are treated, and no denominator is published. Confirmed through KDE's Kentucky Teacher article.

evidence.label: KDE: Kentucky schools show progress toward addressing staffing needs (Oct 2025)

states.what: DESE Educator Vacancy Report (MOSIS October Educator Core, 100% of 556 districts and charters): of 10,380.7 FTE positions that needed filling for 2025-26, 7,982.4 were filled with appropriately certified educators, 1,481.4 with inappropriately certified educators, and 656.1 were left vacant.
states.reason: DESE reports positions left vacant separately from those filled by inappropriately certified educators (temporary and provisional certificates count as appropriate), so the vacant figure is clean. But it pools teachers, counselors, building administrators and superintendents, and DESE gives only a rounded workforce ('approximately 80,000 educators'), so no rate can be computed.

states.what: University system's annual fall unfilled positions survey: 219.3 FTE teachers unfilled in fall 2024 (public, nonpublic, and other entities)
states.reason: Counts from the university system's analysis of districts' fall reporting; no definition of 'unfilled' (or of how substitutes and alternatively licensed teachers are treated) and no denominator; not a state education agency publication.

states.what: SD DOE instructional staff dashboard and dataset: instructional FTE vacant on the first day of school, by district and subject, 2014-15 to 2024-25 (60.2 FTE in 2014-15; 136.7 in 2024-25), with what districts did about each vacancy (e.g., 63.9 FTE 'position remained vacant' in 2024-25).
states.reason: An agency series of first-day vacancies that is not credential-based, but it is derived from the turnover collection (positions left by departing staff), so new positions may be missed; no definition beyond 'vacant at the beginning of the year' and no rate are published. A denominator would have to come from a separate DOE staff count.

evidence.label: SD DOE turnover and vacancy dashboard

states.what: LDOE end-of-year data collection: 736 vacant positions self-reported for 2024-25
states.reason: Counts only, from end-of-year data (the workforce reports used October 1 data before 2021-22); only 22.5% of schools reported vacancies, and no definition was found.

states.what: School boards association fall survey: 205 teacher vacancies as of November 2024
states.reason: Association survey of member districts (161 responding, 43% of enrollment), not an agency; no definition of a vacancy; one year; counts only.

states.what: HIDOE teacher vacancy counts (73 for 2025-26; 142 in Sept 2026; about 1,000 at the fall 2022 peak), as reported in news coverage
states.reason: Counts reported by the department to the press. Emergency hires appear to be counted as filled and substitute-covered positions as vacant, which would be comparable to Illinois and Pennsylvania, but no published series, definition or rate was found.

states.what: RIDE Educator Vacancy Data page: current unfilled positions by district (e.g., Providence 87)
states.reason: Agency counts by district with a download option, but the page gives no definition, source, snapshot date, statewide total or denominator. (LPI lists Rhode Island as publishing no vacancy data.)

states.what: NC School Superintendents' Association survey of district leaders (all 115 districts in 2024 and 2025): K-12 teacher vacancies by level plus exceptional-children teachers, at the start of the year, 2021-2025 (e.g., 581.5 K-5, 446.5 6-8 and 495 9-12 in September 2025); residency-licensed teachers are reported separately.
states.reason: Association survey, not an agency collection; no definition of a vacancy and no denominator. Residency-licensed teachers are counted separately rather than as vacancies.

states.what: KSDE Fall and Spring Vacancy Reports, submitted by every accredited system through the Educator Data Collection System (EDCS): 1,747 'vacancies' in fall 2025 and 1,588 in spring 2026. KSDE also reports positions with no applicants (521 in fall 2025).
states.reason: KSDE's reporting guidance defines a vacancy as 'any position that is not filled' or 'filled with an individual who does not hold an appropriate teaching license for the assignment', including substitute and emergency substitute licenses and teachers lacking the right endorsement (positions held under a waiver, provisional or restricted license, or apprentice license are not vacancies). That pools vacancies with under-credentialed fills, and the truly unfilled positions are not published separately; the no-applicant count is not equivalent, since a position with no applicants may still be covered.

evidence.label: KSDE: Submitting the Fall Vacancy Report (training guide; archived copy)
KSDE: State Board update on educator data, July 2026
HPPR: Kansas reports 9% reduction in classroom teacher vacancies (July 2026)

states.what: NMSU SOAR Center Educator Vacancy Report: open teacher positions advertised on district websites and the REAP job board as of September: 681 (2024-25) and 604 (2025-26).
states.reason: Counts job postings, which can include positions already filled or posted in anticipation, rather than positions districts report as unfilled; a university report, not an agency collection. Not a credential-based measure.

states.what: ALSDE 'Highest Teacher Shortage Areas (as reported by LEAs)': positions in eight shortage fields as of a December snapshot, 1,909.5 (December 2023) and 1,684 (December 2024); a broader 2025-26 count of 3,413 'educator shortage positions' was reported in the press.
states.reason: ALSDE's published tables give no definition, but the department has described the count as positions not filled by a fully certified teacher, including positions held under a substitute license, emergency certificate or temporary CTE certificate and teachers out of field, so it pools vacancies with under-credentialed fills. It also covers the highest shortage areas only, and no denominator is published.

evidence.label: ABC 33/40: Alabama educator shortages jump 23% (definition from ALSDE)

states.what: OPI: 1,039 open education positions listed before 2023-24
states.reason: Job listings, including non-teaching roles; a single year (2023). No newer statewide count from OPI or the Legislature was found.

states.what: DPI Educator Preparation Program Report and Workforce Analysis: licenses with stipulations issued (mostly one-year Tier I licenses for people teaching while completing licensure): 3,016 (2019-20) to 3,734 (2022-23). DPI describes these as positions for which districts 'could not find a qualified Tier II licensed individual to hire.'
states.reason: Not a vacancy count: every position counted is filled, by a teacher who is not yet fully licensed. It contains no unfilled positions, and DPI publishes no statewide count of empty positions.

evidence.label: DPI 2023 Educator Preparation Program and Workforce Analysis Report (Table 26)

states.what: DEED Teacher Vacancy Dashboard (first-day certified vacancy report): teaching positions not filled by someone holding a valid Alaska certificate on the first contract day, with counts and published percentages for 2019-20 through 2025-26 (324 positions, 4.57%, in 2025-26). Counts reported to the Legislature (260 in FY2021 rising to 598 in FY2025) are larger, probably because they cover all certified staff.
states.reason: Counts a position as vacant if its holder lacks a valid Alaska certificate (including expired or still-processing certificates), so the figure pools vacancies with under-certified fills, as in Kansas. DEED does not separate positions that are actually empty. The first contract day also varies by district.

evidence.label: DEED Fall 2026 First Day Certified Vacancy Report Data Handbook

states.what: TDOE Educator Vacancy Report: 1,009 (2022-23), 1,434 (2023-24), about 817-831 (2024-25) teaching positions not filled by a licensed teacher for 20+ days
states.reason: Counts positions not filled by a licensed teacher for 20 or more days, so the figure pools vacancies with positions covered by substitutes or unlicensed staff, as in Alaska and Kansas. A statewide rate ('just under 2%' for 2023-24) appears only in secondary coverage, and the State Board PDF could not be retrieved automatically.

states.what: MDE Educator Shortage Survey (100% of districts, Aug 13 to Nov 1, 2025): teacher vacancies 3,036 (2021-22), 2,593, 2,775, 2,964, 3,815 (2025-26)
states.reason: MDE's reports (2022, 2024, 2025) do not define a vacancy, but secondary sources describe the measure as classes without a licensed and certified teacher: the 2021-22 baseline of just over 3,000 was reported as positions 'either completely vacant or held by teachers who were not properly certified.' That pools vacancies with under-certified fills, as in Alaska, Tennessee and Kansas, and fits the counts' size (roughly 12% of the teacher workforce in 2025-26). Counts are also reported as of varying dates across a 2.5-month window, and no yearly denominator is published.

evidence.label: MDE Educator Workforce Shortages and Strategies, Dec 2025
MDE 2024-25 Educator Shortage Survey Results and Strategies, Dec 2024
Magnolia Tribune: MDE defines a teacher vacancy as a class without a licensed and certified teacher (Dec 2024)
Proxlearn summary of 2021 baseline (vacant or not properly certified)

states.what: Commission on Teacher Credentialing assignment-monitoring dashboard (CalSAAS): a multi-year statewide count of 'vacancies', defined as 'assignments identified within the system as not having a certificated employee permanently assigned on census date,' reported separately from misassignments. Also CDE's 'Estimated Number of Teacher Hires' (projected hires) and a one-time Commission figure of 10,000+ vacancies in 2021-22.
states.reason: The CalSAAS vacancy category is not credential-based (misassignments are counted separately), but it counts assignments, not positions: one educator can hold several assignments, and some instructional modes count students as assignments, so it cannot be set beside position-based vacancy rates. CDE's figure is projected hiring demand, not unfilled positions. Analysts' shortage estimates based on substandard credentials and permits count filled positions.

evidence.label: CTC California Educator Assignment Monitoring dashboard

states.what: New law (ORC 3301.82, effective Sept 30, 2025) requires the Department of Education and Workforce to collect vacancy data annually from Sept 30, 2026, and publish it, including positions filled by long-term substitutes, unlicensed or emergency-credentialed staff, and positions left unfilled.
states.reason: Watch for the first publication (likely 2027). Potentially a strong addition.

states.what: New TSDS Teacher Vacancy Collection (HB 2) starting 2026-27: all vacant teaching positions Sept 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027, whether or not later filled
states.reason: No figures yet; first results expected after the 2026-27 year.

evidence.label: TEA: New TSDS Core Collection: Teacher Vacancy Collection

states.what: Maine DOE now asks districts to certify teacher and educational technician vacancy data each fall (from October 1); LD 2015 (2026) proposed making annual reporting statutory
states.reason: No published statewide figures found yet.

states.what: NJSLEDS Staff Vacancy collection (required by N.J.S.A. 18A:27-3.5 to 3.7): vacant, new, and eliminated teaching positions each year
states.reason: Results are said to feed the Commissioner's annual staffing report, but no published statewide figures were found.

states.what: NYSED Educator Vacancy and Hiring Survey, annually February to July
states.reason: Results inform state policy but no published statewide figures were found.

evidence.label: NYSED Educator Vacancy and Hiring Survey

states.what: NHED annual survey of vacancies by endorsement (previous year, plus positions open in mid-August), used for the Critical Shortage List
states.reason: Publishes shortage designations, not vacancy counts.

states.what: State law requires IDOE to collect teacher vacancy data and report it in a Teacher Statistics Report; IDOE's job board counts postings (about 2,200 teaching postings in June 2024)
states.reason: The statutory report could not be found and has lagged; job-board counts are postings, a different measure.

evidence.label: IEERB annual report noting the report's absence

states.what: Annual teacher workforce report covers shortage areas, pipeline and retention
states.reason: No statewide vacancy counts found.

states.what: Educator Pipeline dashboards (personnel, not vacancies)
states.reason: No statewide vacancy counts found.

states.what: Educator Pipeline Report (attrition, authorizations); a one-time 2016 superintendent survey
states.reason: No current statewide vacancy counts.

evidence.label: FY25 Educator Pipeline Report (State Board page; the original PDF link now returns 404)
FY25 Educator Pipeline Report PDF (Internet Archive copy, April 2026)

states.what: Staffing and licensure data by district
states.reason: No statewide vacancy counts found.

states.what: Turnover data and emergency-certification rules
states.reason: No statewide vacancy counts found.

evidence.label: OSDE interim study on teacher shortage (2021)

states.what: Educator Equity Report: share of positions vacated each year (a turnover measure)
states.reason: Turnover, not unfilled positions.

states.what: Criticality index (share of positions not filled by fully qualified staff), exit surveys
states.reason: USBE does not publish a statewide count of open positions.

states.what: Agency uses job postings (SchoolSpring) as a proxy
states.reason: The agency says it does not collect position-level shortage data.

states.what: PESB shortage display (limited certificates, out-of-endorsement)
states.reason: OSPI's 2025 legislative report says it has no vacancy numbers.

states.what: Counts of uncertified or underprepared teachers
states.reason: WVDE reports that it does not publish vacancy counts.

evidence.label: WVDE Education Preparation Task Force Report

states.what: Legislative studies of teacher labor markets
states.reason: A 2023 legislative report lists Wyoming among states with no vacancy data; 2025 testimony still recommends building it.

evidence.label: Monitoring Markets and Recruiting Quality Teachers in Wyoming (2023)
